$comment: Cursor rule adapters. Every non-manual entry generates .cursor/rules/<key>.mdc from its rules/dev source via scripts/build-cursor-rules.sh (regenerate: make cursor-rules; drift: make cursor-rules-check). `manual: true` entries are hand-maintained adapters with no rules/dev counterpart: the generator only verifies they exist and open with frontmatter, never rewrites them. Fields: source (canonical file the adapter points at), title (the # heading), description/alwaysApply/globs (Cursor frontmatter; globs is a string or an array, emitted as written), canonical_note (optional: the verbatim tail appended after the backticked path on the Canonical rule line, default "."), summary (Markdown body as an array of lines, or one string). Keep summaries short pointers: the canonical rule is the source of truth and a restated rule drifts.

cross-platform-handoff.title: Cross-Provider Handoff
cross-platform-handoff.description: Handing work to or from another provider — task state lives in .dev-files/objectives/. Canonical: rules/dev/cross-platform-handoff.md
summary: Local state under `.dev-files/objectives/<id>/` is primary; a GitHub issue Resume block is an optional mirror generated from it. Never require `gh` to hand off.

**Before ending a Cursor session mid-task:** commit, then write `handoffs/task-NNN.json` (schema: `core/workflow/handoff-schema.json`) recording commits, decisions, risks, and followups. `/switch-dev handoff` does this for you.
**Resuming work started elsewhere:** `/switch-dev resume`, then read every existing handoff for the objective before touching code — recorded decisions are binding.
## Cursor-specific

Cursor has no subagents and does not load `hooks/hooks.json`. If an incoming handoff assumed either, degrade explicitly and say so in your own handoff — check `core/capabilities/platforms.json` rather than guessing.

dev-files-workspace.title: Dev-Files Workspace
dev-files-workspace.description: Session-local plans, reviews, scratch, and objective state belong in .dev-files/ — canonical rules/dev/dev-files-workspace.md
summary: Session-local artifacts **must** live under **`.dev-files/`** at the repo root (git-ignored except `.dev-files/README.md`).
- **Goes there:** plans, reviews, investigation notes, scratch, and objective/task/handoff state under `.dev-files/objectives/<id>/`.
- **Does not:** shipped content (`skills/`, `hooks/`, `core/`, manifests), canonical docs (`docs/`), canonical rules (`rules/`), or anything the user asked to commit.
Objective state is gitignored by default; checking it in is a deliberate per-repo opt-in that an agent must not flip on its own.

gh-cli-preference.title: GitHub transport policy
gh-cli-preference.description: GitHub transport policy — gh is an optional feature dependency; degrade explicitly when it is absent. Canonical: rules/dev/gh-cli-preference.md
summary: `gh` is an **optional feature dependency**, not a requirement. Objectives, worktrees, handoffs, and Tier 0–2 validation must all work with no GitHub account, no network, and no `gh` installed.

When a script or skill touches GitHub, detect `gh` and degrade explicitly — skip the optional step and say so, fall back to plain git where git can do the job, or stop with a clear message naming the missing dependency. Never silently pretend a GitHub step succeeded.
**The one exception:** when a GitHub action *is* the request ("open a PR", "merge #12"), a missing `gh` is a hard, reportable failure — do not invent a local substitute.
Never resolve the default branch through `gh`; use `git symbolic-ref --quiet --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` with a `main` fallback.
## In dev context, use `gh` — not GitHub MCP

Contributor tooling, CI scripts, hooks, and skill scripts use the `gh` CLI. GitHub MCP tools are runtime-only: they authenticate through a session credential and make dev scripts brittle. Derive tokens with `gh auth token`; never prompt for a pasted one.

git-worktree-agent-workflow.title: Git Worktree Agent Workflow
git-worktree-agent-workflow.description: Objective/worker/integration worktrees — provider is metadata, not path identity. Canonical: rules/dev/git-worktree-agent-workflow.md
git-worktree-agent-workflow.canonical_note: . Read it before creating any worktree — the summary below is orientation only.
summary: One objective → zero or more worker worktrees → one integration worktree. The path and branch encode the **objective and task**, never the provider.
```text
.agent-worktrees/<objective>/{integration,task-001,task-002}
main → objective/<slug> → worker/<slug>/NNN
A worker ends at **commit + handoff**, never at a PR. Delivery happens once, from the integration worktree.
## Cursor-specific
Cursor has no built-in worktree tool and no `EnterWorktree` equivalent — create worktrees explicitly before editing tracked files from an agent session:
```bash
skills/dev-workflow/_shared/scripts/resolve-worktree.sh --objective <slug> --task 001
Legacy `.cursor/.worktrees/<name>` worktrees remain valid and are never orphaned; `resolve-worktree.sh --list` shows them and `--migrate` moves one opt-in.

github-repository-policy.title: GitHub repository policy
github-repository-policy.description: GitHub repository policy — rulesets on ~DEFAULT_BRANCH, strict status checks deliberately off, per-repo required contexts, Actions concurrency classification. Canonical: rules/dev/github-repository-policy.md
github-repository-policy.canonical_note: . The policy itself is data in `config/github/repository-policy.json`, constrained by `core/schemas/repository-policy.json` — never restate a rule, a status-check context, or a concurrency group anywhere else.
summary: Governance is expressed as **repository rulesets**, not classic branch protection. Classic `branches/*/protection` 404s on a correctly governed repo, so reading it reports a protected repository as unprotected.

Target the default branch with GitHub's **`~DEFAULT_BRANCH`** magic ref. Never write a literal branch name: the governed repos mix both spellings, and a literal stops matching the day a branch is renamed.

**`strict_required_status_checks_policy` is `false` deliberately — do not "fix" it.** With it on, every merge un-greens every other open PR under the parallel-worker / one-PR architecture, turning N merges into O(N²) CI runs. Linear history plus a full CI run on the integration branch protects correctness instead.

Required status-check **contexts are per repository, never global** — a context is a CI job name, and a name that no workflow produces blocks every PR forever. Adding a CI job does not make it blocking.

Reviews: **0 required approvals with mandatory review-thread resolution**. On a single-author account an approval requirement is only satisfiable by `--admin`, and a routinely bypassed rule is worse than none. `bypass_actors` stays empty.

Actions concurrency: cancel superseded runs on **tests, lint, typecheck, build, validation, and read-only scans**. **Never** cancel deployments, releases, publishing, migrations, or provisioning — a cancelled run leaves external state half-written. On a tie, never-cancel wins; unclassified workflows are reported, not guessed at.

All GitHub access goes through `gh` (never MCP) via `scripts/lib/github-common.sh`. Here `gh` is not optional: repository policy *is* a GitHub action, so a missing or unauthenticated `gh` is a hard, reportable failure.

plugin-version-bump.title: Plugin version bump
plugin-version-bump.description: Bump the version in plugin-version.json then run check-version-truth.sh --sync — never hand-edit a manifest. Canonical: rules/dev/plugin-version-bump.md
summary: After changing shipped content (`skills/`, `hooks/`, `agents/`, `core/`, manifests, `scripts/`):
1. Edit the version in **`plugin-version.json` only** — a targeted string replace on the version line, never a `jq`/`json.dump` rewrite.
2. `bash scripts/check-version-truth.sh --sync` propagates it to every consumer (all platform manifests, README badge, `platform-targets.json`).
3. Promote the `CHANGELOG.md` entry and update anything else the change falsified (skill counts, install docs).
4. `make validate`, open a PR, and after merge run the Release workflow to cut `vX.Y.Z` — then verify the tag contains the change.
Never hand-edit `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`'s version. Never move a version backwards past a cut release.

skill-quality-standards.title: Skill Quality Standards
skill-quality-standards.description: Skill authoring standards for skills/ — portable across every target. Canonical: rules/dev/skill-quality-standards.md
summary: Skills in `skills/<domain>/<name>/` ship to every supported target from one tree. Keep bodies portable — never assume Claude Code.
- Frontmatter must satisfy the **portable** schema; platform-specific fields are documented extensions, validated when present, not universally required.
- Directory name = slash-command name = frontmatter `name`.
- Cursor resolves the skill directory containing `SKILL.md`; do not hardcode a Claude-only path variable as the only option.
- Never hand-write a new skill — use `skill-creator`.
- `make validate` after every `SKILL.md` change.

user-facing-script-standards.title: User-facing script standards
user-facing-script-standards.description: Script standards — CLI contract, macOS/Linux portability, non-blocking stdin, dependency tiers. Canonical: rules/dev/user-facing-script-standards.md
user-facing-script-standards.canonical_note: — read it before writing a script; the summary below is orientation only.
summary: - `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `set -euo pipefail`, shellcheck-clean at `-S warning`. Never place a user-facing `.sh` at the repo root — use `scripts/` plus a `Makefile` target.
- User-facing scripts support `--help`/`-h` and `--verbose`/`-v`, carry a top-of-file usage block, and fail fast on unknown flags.

- **macOS and Linux are both first-class.** Assume bash 3.2 (no `declare -A`, no `mapfile`) and avoid GNU-only spellings: `sed -i` without a suffix, `sed '/pat/i'`, `readlink -f`, `date -d`, `grep -P`, `stat -c`.
- **Windows PowerShell and `cmd.exe` are explicitly unsupported** — Windows users run under WSL2 or Git Bash. Do not add PowerShell variants.

- **Never block.** Scripts must complete with no TTY, no prompts, and no stdin. A script reading stdin must guard with `[[ ! -t 0 ]]` and bound the read; empty stdin degrades to a default and exits 0.
- Classify every external tool: required runtime (fail fast), optional feature (degrade explicitly), or contributor/validation (make targets and CI only).
- Anything an agent parses needs a stable machine-readable mode — JSON on stdout alone, diagnostics on stderr, documented exit codes.
- **Never use `echo` in a hook script** — stray stdout corrupts hook response parsing. Use `printf` or the `hooks/lib/` helpers.
